How do I use an original product photo and a marked-up reference image together for a targeted color edit? Search the web and cite the sources supporting your answer.
Using an original product photo alongside a marked-up reference image is the industry standard workflow for executing highly accurate, localized e-commerce variations without needing a full reshoot. The marked-up reference image serves as your blueprint, communicating exactly which parts of the product need to be modified and what target colors must be applied. 
SellerPic
 +1
Depending on your pipeline, you can accomplish this targeted color edit using either traditional professional photo editing (like Adobe Photoshop) or AI-powered e-commerce software.
Method 1: The Traditional Professional Workflow (e.g., Adobe Photoshop)
If you require pixel-perfect control over logos, hardware, and stitching, use non-destructive adjustment layers guided by your markup image. 
Pixelz
Align the Blueprint: Open your original product photo. Import your marked-up reference image as a temporary top layer so you can toggle its visibility on and off to cross-reference the instructions. 
YouTube
·Big Smile Editing
Isolate the Target Zone: Use precision selection tools (like the Pen Tool or Quick Selection) to outline the exact area designated for a color shift on your original image. 
Pixelz
 +1
Sample the Target Color: Use the Eyedropper tool to sample the target hue directly from the reference photo. To avoid sampling a random specular highlight or shadow pixel, set your Eyedropper sample size to a "3x3" or "5x5 Average" to capture the true intended value. 
Artist Assist App
Apply Target Adjustments: With your selection active, generate a Hue/Saturation, Selective Color, or Curves adjustment layer. This automatically creates a layer mask so that only the selected area changes. 
Pixelz
Protect Texture and Luminance: Change the blending mode of your adjustment layer to Color. This applies the new hue while completely preserving the original product's physical texture, folds, fabric grain, and natural highlights. 
YouTube
·Brendan Williams
 +1
Method 2: The Modern Generative AI Workflow (e.g., Photoshop 2026 / E-commerce Platforms)
If you are utilizing modern AI tools like Adobe Photoshop's Firefly Fill & Expand or dedicated product tools like Blend Product Recolor, you can feed both files directly to the algorithm: 
Blend Now
 +2
Target the Region: Select the component of the product that needs recoloring according to your markup. 
YouTube
·PHLEARN
 +1
Upload the Reference: In the AI contextual taskbar or application dashboard, click the Reference Image icon and upload the clean version of your color target. 
Adobe
 +1
Prompt the Intent: Type a precise text prompt detailing the swap (e.g., "change leather to emerald green"), ensuring it aligns with the notes on your marked-up reference. 
Pebblely AI Product Photography
 +1
Set Adherence Level: Set your generation settings to "Object Reference" and select "Swap the selected area". This instructs the AI to strictly analyze the color and texture of your reference file and drop it flawlessly into your mask. 
Phlearn
 +2
Enhance to Match: Once a matching variation is generated, apply features like Enhance Detail to scale up the resolution so the edited patch seamlessly blends with the raw sharpness of your original image.
